figures.finding: UK and Ireland 2023 box office by BFI primary genre: action 26.7% of gross from 16.4% of 900 releases, animation 19.6% from 6.1%, drama 15.8% from 35.6%, comedy 15.4% from 18.6%, horror 7.1% from 4.1%, documentary 0.3% from 9.4%; total £994.3 million.

value.unit: share of gross box office and of releases

figures.applies: UK and Republic of Ireland theatrical releases, calendar 2023 (figures at 4 February 2024; table corrected 3 July 2026); latest BFI yearbook edition (2024).
figures.use: A film's UK box office draws on its genre's share of gross per release here; the BFI's genre list (18 genres) maps to the game's genres by name.

figures.finding: Of 4,403 actors under 35 in US films of 2000-2025 whose family status could be confirmed, 28% (1,242) had at least one parent who worked in entertainment; of those, 60% had a parent in acting, 16% directing, 14% music, 9% producing, and 41% had two industry parents.

value.by_year: about 6-8% of young casts in the 2000s and 2010s, 16.6% by 2024 (as the report states)

figures.applies: Actors under 35 at release in US films 2000-2025 meeting a visibility criterion; a data company's own sample, which says it does not represent all working actors.
figures.use: Which trade an actor's industry parent had (acting most often) is drawn from these shares; a cross-check on Follows's 28% for stars.

sources.said: From 2000 to 2025, nepo babies made up 28% of confirmed young actors in U.S. movies, while 72% were non-nepo stars.
Directing was the second most common connection at 16%, followed by the music sector at 14% and producing at 9%.
Most nepo stars came from one-industry-parent households: 59% had one parent in entertainment, while 41% had two parents in the entertainment industry.
The confirmed-status sample included 4,403 actors under age 35, of whom 1,242 were confirmed nepo actors.

figures.finding: Gorji, Carney and Prakash (2020) find, on IMDb data for Hollywood show-business families, strong support that third-party network sponsorship benefits relatives' careers, more so for women, alongside the continuing importance of direct family preferment.

value.effect: sponsorship by family associates significantly benefits relatives' career performance; accentuated for women; direct preferment also matters

figures.applies: Hollywood movie industry, show-business family relatives (abstract only; the full text is paywalled).
figures.use: A family in the business works through the people the family knows (a contact who sponsors the player), which is how the game's contacts engine should carry it.

sources.said: We find strong support for our sponsorship hypotheses, but we also note the continuing importance of direct forms of family preferment in an industry characterized by single project organizations and boundaryless careers.
